Tuned for coding agents. Suppresses encoding rules and the pipe-to-shell command rule that fire on legitimate code (base64, homoglyphs, pipe-to-shell), raises the confidence floor to 0.6, downgrades the three ML prompt-injection verdicts (LLM Guard's petasos.llmguard.injection, LlamaFirewall's petasos.llamafirewall.prompt-guard, and PromptGuard's petasos.promptguard.injection) to non-blocking, and direction-scopes the syntactic injection floor (injection_floor_scope=inbound) so the agent's own outbound tool calls may carry injection-shaped text as data. Those ML classifiers flag ordinary outbound tool calls (ls, curl, git status, file searches over security docs, heredocs that process attack strings as data) as injection at confidence 0.5-1.0, so the 0.6 floor cannot tame them; the overrides keep the findings visible for audit (still logged at low, and still counted toward session frequency/escalation, so an armed session may sit at a non-blocking tier1) without blocking. The syntactic injection, role-switch, and agent-directive rules are suppressed on outbound only: an inbound injection attempt (someone trying to manipulate THIS model) still blocks at full strength under this profile. Unlike the ML downgrades, a suppressed outbound injection is dropped before merge: it leaves only a debug-log trace, does not appear in the audit spool, and is not counted toward frequency or escalation. For: code-writing and dev-tooling agents on a trusted operator's own machine. Trade-off: pipe-to-shell stays suppressed, so a bare ... | sh with no fetch or decode stage is not a Petasos finding under this profile (Hermes's own approval patterns still prompt on that literal form); curl/wget ... | sh and base64 -d ... | sh still fire fetch-exec / decode-exec and route to Hermes approval. The other four command rules (destructive-recursive, fetch-exec, decode-exec, alias-escape) stay active. With dangerous_tool_posture=approve they route a dangerous tool call to Hermes approval instead of a Petasos quarantine, keyed by the worst command finding; an unanswered or denied approval fails closed in Hermes. Under YOLO, or on a host without the approve directive, those same findings block. ML prompt-injection on tool-call params no longer blocks, and outbound syntactic injection no longer blocks. The ML injection downgrades are direction-blind, so if this profile is ever used on an inbound surface, ML injection blocking is off there too; the syntactic injection relaxation is direction-scoped, but it is only safe if the host labels untrusted content direction=inbound (the per-call default falls back to config.direction, so keep that set to inbound), and second-order egress (an induced outbound attack payload) is guarded by the egress fence (PET-134/133/112) where that fence is deployed; if it is not present, the second-order egress path is uncovered, so arm this profile only if you accept that residual. Still blocking: structural anomalies (unsuppressible on every direction), inbound syntactic injection, role-switch, and agent-directive rules, Presidio PII egress (PET-135, PET-162), source-taint egress, non-command HIGH findings, and tier-2 or tier-3 escalation.

import asyncio, json, sys, time
sys.path[:] = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
from petasos.scanners._semgrep_source import (
    _FENCE, _is_header, _is_search_header, preflight, select_sources,
)

async def run():
    values = {
        "header": "def f(" + ")->x" * 249970,
        "header_colon": "def f(" + ")->x" * 249960 + ":!:",
        "search": "a" + "." * 999850 + "\rb\neval(x)",
        "fence": "`" * 999850 + "\rX\neval(x)",
    }
    measured = {}
    for name, body in values.items():
        for wrapped in (False, True):
            text = json.dumps(body) if wrapped else body
            started = time.perf_counter()
            assert not _is_header(body)
            assert not _is_search_header(body)
            assert not list(_FENCE.finditer(body))
            assert await preflight(text)
            selected = await select_sources(text)
            assert selected.examined == len(text)
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
            measured[name + ("_json" if wrapped else "_raw")] = elapsed
            assert elapsed < 2.0, (name, wrapped, elapsed)
    print(json.dumps(measured))

asyncio.run(run())

import asyncio, json, sys, time
sys.path[:] = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
from petasos.scanners._semgrep_source import _is_candidate, preflight, select_sources

async def run():
    dotted = "a." * 499950
    values = {
        "raw": dotted,
        "json": json.dumps(dotted),
        "after_fence": "```python\neval(x)\n```\n" + dotted,
        "json_after_call": json.dumps(["eval(x)", dotted]),
    }
    measured = {}
    for name, text in values.items():
        started = time.perf_counter()
        assert not _is_candidate(dotted)
        # A leading marker defeats the cheap absence check, exercising the
        # maximal-run matcher on the entire hostile identifier as well.
        assert not _is_candidate("(" + dotted)
        gate = await preflight(text)
        selection = await select_sources(text)
        expected = name in ("after_fence", "json_after_call")
        assert gate is expected, name
        assert len(selection.targets) == int(expected), name
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
        measured[name] = elapsed
        assert elapsed < 1.0, (name, elapsed)
    print(json.dumps(measured))

asyncio.run(run())
